body:
N-26 SLICES 1 AND 2 ARE BUILT, NOT WALKED, NOT MARKED (helper-n26, 15 Nov 2026). The item is not complete (slices 3 to 5 and N-28 remain; RELEASE-CANDIDATE 4b needs 1 and 2 in the first public image: both are built). I did not run `roadmap.py mark`.

SLICE 1 AMENDMENT (found on the real stack by the lead, 14 Nov): two REMOVED UPLOADS (Nneka - Heartbeat, Foals - Full Performance: videoType None, isAvailable False, no album, artists [KEXP]) were filed under KEXP because the reader took "no videoType and unavailable" for a removed catalogue song. Only an ALBUM says that now. Recorded (tests/fixtures/ytm/n26/kexp_removed_uploads.get_playlist.json). First commit of the slice 2 branch.

SLICE 2 (migration 0014, song_ref.artist_basis + uploader, nullable, NOTHING else: no default/check/update):
- NULL = "as before" = a performer, NEVER `channel`. Old rows and phone/file/scan refs keep NULL. Value checked in refs (a 5th basis needs no table rebuild). Not sent to phones (docs/17 unchanged, tested).
- Set by the importer only (refs.resolve keyword arguments; a client's artistBasis/uploader is ignored at POST refs/resolve and the file import, tested). A nameless song is `unknown` whatever the reader says.
- FACTS ARE ONLY FILLED, NEVER REWRITTEN (refs.facts_to_fill, one rule for _enrich and the merge repair): the design says only "fills a null basis only when the artist agrees"; a set basis is never changed by a stronger or weaker reading (an upgrade = slice 5 / N-28, with the artist rewrite). The basis fills only when the reading names the same artist; `channel`/`unknown` only when the ref plays from the very video the reading came from (a performer's catalogue ref found by name for an upload on the band's own channel must not be downgraded).
- UPLOADER = the channel of the upload the ref was made from. A NEW ref stores it whatever the video (the design's definition has no video; removed uploads have none). ALTERNATIVE: only with a video. COST of the choice: a later search may attach another video, the uploader stays the original's. A ref FOUND takes it only when it plays from that very video.
- refmerge: both columns in _NOT_COPIED, same rule.
- NEVER SENT TO THE CATALOGUE for `channel`/`unknown` (or the placeholder name): artist_finder (a name is asked about only with its performer/NULL songs; all channel = skipped), cover_finder (left out of _wanting) and the keeper's cover step (reads the basis from the row). COST: a band's own-channel upload loses a catalogue cover until N-28 and keeps its video thumbnail (the lead's "never"; overrule = performer_clause in cover_finder._wanting and keeper._may_ask_the_catalogue). SQL is (col IS NULL OR col NOT IN ...): a bare NOT IN drops every NULL row.

STILL OPEN: slice 3 (no artist page for a channel: a proof on the real music server first), slice 4 (ARTE Concert, Crunchyroll), slice 5 (repair of stored rows, trigger-gated), N-28 (catalogue names the artist of a `channel` song). Leftovers, all pinned by named tests: an OMV credited to a label with no separator keeps the label; an upload whose title names nobody keeps its uploader flagged `channel`; a description with the placeholder and NO id is a new ref each time.
